discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Higgs mechanism, but the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 has not been recognised. It was only possible because Peter Jenni (ATLAS) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (CMS) conceived, designed and led the construction of general-purpose detectors of unprecedented scale and precision. Their key design choices were high-resolution electromagnetic calorimetry, precise muon systems and hermetic coverage. These made the diphoton and four-lepton channels sensitive enough to see a narrow resonance at 125 GeV. The detectors have since turned the Higgs into a precision laboratory: couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and now muons are measured, and those measurements constrain effective field theories of physics beyond the Standard Model. Few instruments have changed what we can learn from data about the electroweak scale so much.
